title: Module 6 Knowledge Check
description: Ten questions on strategies, multimedia, accessibility, and prototyping. Unlimited attempts; best score counts.

questions.text: A lesson presents content clearly and ends with a summary, but learners never practice or receive feedback. In Gagne's terms this lesson is missing:
questions.feedback: Eliciting performance (6) and providing feedback (7) are what make it instruction rather than presentation.

questions.text: Which practices are supported by the cognitive research summarized in this module? Select all that apply.
options: Rereading as the main study method
Studying worked examples before solving problems as a novice
questions.feedback: Retrieval, spacing, interleaving, and worked examples with fading are well supported. Rereading is weak.

questions.text: Clark's argument that 'media will never influence learning' implies that designers should:
options: Choose media after deciding the method, based on what the method requires
questions.feedback: Methods cause learning; media constrain which methods are feasible. Choose media to serve the events and practice the strategy requires.

questions.text: A narrated video shows a diagram while the same sentences appear as on-screen text. Which of Mayer's principles does this violate?
questions.feedback: Presenting identical words as narration and on-screen text overloads the verbal channel. Narrate the diagram; keep captions as an accessibility option.

questions.text: Which is an example of the UDL principle of multiple means of action and expression?
options: Offering a choice of product format where the objective allows
Making the relevance of the topic explicit
questions.feedback: Choice of how to demonstrate learning is action and expression. Captions and glossaries are representation; relevance is engagement.

questions.text: Which items belong on the accessibility checklist for an e-learning asset? Select all that apply.
questions.feedback: Alt text, captions, keyboard operability, and real headings. Background music violates Mayer's coherence principle and can interfere with screen readers.

questions.text: The minimum WCAG color contrast ratio for normal text at level AA is 4.5:1.
You want to test whether the sequence and decision points of a branching scenario make sense before spending days in an authoring tool. What fidelity of prototype should you use?
options: Medium fidelity in the authoring tool
Paper or low fidelity (index cards, text-only, or clickable slides)
No prototype; write a longer design document
questions.feedback: Start at the lowest fidelity that answers the question. Sequence and logic can be tested on paper.

questions.text: Where should the wrong options in a branching scenario's decision screens come from?
options: The common errors recorded at branch points in the task analysis
questions.feedback: Real errors make realistic, diagnostic distractors and connect the practice to the performance.

questions.text: Which standard packages an authoring-tool module so an LMS can track completion and score?
questions.feedback: SCORM (or xAPI with a learning record store). Common Cartridge exchanges whole courses between LMSs.
